פאר.def:
H6287. p

'er מְּאֵר‎ noun masculineEzek 44:18 head-dress, turban (? originally ornament); — absolute ׳פ‎ of bridegroom Isa 61:10, sign of joy 61:3 (opposed to mourning, and so) מְּאֵרְךָ‎ Ezek 24:17, plural suffix מְּאֵרֵכֶם‎ 24:23 (worn by men of position); of priests פִשְׁתִּים מַּאֲרֵי‎ 44:18, שֵׁשׁמּ ׳הַמִּנְבָּעֹת‎ Exod 39:28 (P); plural absolute מְּאֵרִים‎ Isa 3:20 (of luxurious women).

H6288. porah

H6289. parur

פארן.def:
H6290. Paran

פגול.def:
H6292. piggul

[מִּגּוּל‎] noun masculineLev 7:18 foul thing, refuse, but only as technical term of unclean sacrificial flesh; — it is ׳פ‎ if eaten on third day 7:18 (P), 19:7 (H); compare פ ׳בְּשַׂר‎ Ezek 4:14 (undefined); plural מִּגֻּלִים מְרַק‎ Isa 65:4 broth of refuse things (Kt פרק‎), RSSem i. 325, 2nd ed. 343 thinks of flesh with the blood; Duon the passage of mice and other unclean animals.

פגע.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

פגר.def:
H6296. pagar

[מָּגַר‎] verb Pi`el be exhausted, faint (מְּגַר ᵑ7‎ derived species tear down, destroy; Assyrian pagru, body, corpse; Late Hebrew מֶּגֶר‎ = Biblical Hebrew; Aramaic מַּגְרָא‎, ; Palmyrene פגר‎; Mandean פאגרא‎ NöM § 89); — Perfect3plural מִן מִּגְּרוּ‎ they were too faint to go, etc. 1Sam 30:10, 21.

פגש.def:
H7971. shalach

I. שָׁלַח‎844 verb send (Late Hebrew id.; Ecclus 48:18 +; Aramaic שְׁלַךְ‎, , SoBuhl BaEs 41 compare Arabic (r = l), send forth, drive cattle to pasture, send messenger, etc., but then different √ for I. שֶׁלַךְ‎, Arabic , weapon; Assyrian probably šalû (send, hurl?), whence tešlitu, command); —

Qal562 Perfect3masculine singular ׳שׁ‎ Gen 42:4 2masculine singular suffix שְׁלַחְתָּ֑נִי‎ Exod 5:22, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יִשְׁלַח‎ Gen 3:22 +, 2 feminine plural תִּשְׁלַ֫חְנָה‎ Ezek 23:40 (Judg 5:26 read תִּשְׁלָחֶנָּה‎? Ges § 47 k); Imperative masculine singular שְׁלַךְ‎ 1Sam 20:31 +, masculine plural שְׁלָ֑חוּ‎ 2Kin 2:17; Infinitive abs. שָׁל(וֺ)ךְַ‎ Num 22:37 +; construct שְׁלֹתַ‎ 22:15 +, שְׁלַךְ‎ Isa 58:9, suffix שָׁלְחֶ֑ךָ‎ Gen 38:17 etc.; Participle act. שֹׁלֵךְַ‎ Exod 9:14 +, etc.; שָׁלוּחַ‎ 1Kin 14:6 +, etc., —

1 send: human subject, especially

a. accusative of person Gen 42:4; 43:8 (both J; with אֵת‎ with, person) Num 22:15 (E) + often, with ל‎ of thing for which Jer 14:3; followed by אֶל‎ person Gen 37:13(J), 2Sam 11:6; Neh 6:5 +; rarely with ל‎ person Gen 32:19 (J; pass.), אֶל‎, of location 2Chr 16:4, ב‎ of location 1Sam 11:3, ל‎ of location 1 Kings 5:28, accusative of location 2Kin 22:3, ה‎- locative + מֵעַל‎ person 2Sam 13:17, מִן‎ local Gen 37:14 (J), Num 13:3 (P), etc.; followed by infinitive purpose 1Sam 25:14 ( + מִן‎ local), 2Kin 1:16; Jer 40:14 +, אֶל‎ person with infinitive purpose 2Sam 10:3; Jer 42:9 +, with ו‎ subordinate 2Kin 5:6, with finite verb actionis Exod 2:5 (E), sent her maid and took, +, etc. (many combinations); accusative of person alone 24:5 (E), Josh 7:22(E), 2Sam 10:7 +?

b. less often accusative of thing (sometimes with בְּיַד‎ of agent), with אֶל‎ person 1Sam 16:20; 2Kin 5:5; 20:12 +, 1 Kings 5:23 (= designate by sending unto), ל‎ person Judg 3:15; 1 Kings 5:22 +, אֶל‎ location Est 1:22, שָׁ֫מָּה‎ 2Kin 6:14; + infinitive purpose 1Chr 19:4; Est 4:4; + finite verb action. Psa 105:28; accusative of kid, alone, Gen 38:23 also (accusative omitted) 38:17, etc.

c. very oft,. without object: + finite verb action., send and do so and so, Gen 27:45(E), 2Kin 11:14; Job 1:5 +; with אֶל‎ person Hosea 5:13; 2Sam 11:6 +, especially + לֵאמֹר‎ Gen 38:25(J), 1Kin 20:5 (often in Samuel Kings), Jer 29:28 +; with infinitive purpose Gen 32:6 (J), Num 21:32 (J), 1Sam 22:11 +, etc. (and so 31:9 reading וַיִּשְׁלְחוּ‎, for

Pi`el, Th We Dr Now, not HPS Bu); absolute 2Kin 2:16-17, 2Sam 14:29; = send to inquire 1Kin 20:17, etc.

2 send: subject ׳י‎ (God),

a. accusative of person Gen 45:5; (E; לִפְנֵי‎ person), 1Sam 15:18 (בְּדָ֑רֶךְ‎), + אֶל‎ person 2Sam 12:1; accusative of angel, לִפְנֵי‎ person Gen 24:7; Exod 33:2 (both J), אֵת‎ with Gen 24:40(J), etc.; with accusative of person = commission Exod 3:12 (E), Judg 6:14; Isa 6:8; Jer 14:14-15, +? Jeremiah; Zech 2:13 +; also (with אֶל‎ person) Exod 3:13 (E), Jer 25:4; Ezek 3:6 +, etc.; especially of sending prophet, (שָׁלַךְ‎), וְשָׁלוֺחַ הַשְׁכֵּם‎ Jer 7:25 + (see [שָׁרַם‎]); accusative of person + infinitive purpose 1Sam 15:1; Jer 19:14 +; + עַד‎ location 2Kin 2:2, accusative of location 2:4, ָ  ה‎ locative 2:6, etc.

b. with accusative of thing, plagues Exod 9:14 (with ב אֶללֵֿב,‎ person), figurative arrows 2Sam 22:15 = Psa 18:15( + verb finite action.), 144:6, compare Jer 25:16 and elsewhere; his word Isa 9:7 (ב‎ of a people), 55:11 (אשׁר‎ to which), Zech 7:12 (ב‎ agent.), Psa 107:20 (+ finite verb action.), 147:15 (+ accusative אֶרֶץ‎); accusative help 20:3 (מִן‎ local), light and truth 43:3 (+ finite verb action.), compare 57:4

3 stretch out, especially accusative hand:

a. human subject, with ב‎ person against, Gen 37:22(E), 1Sam 24:11; Est 2:21+; with ב‎ of thing (property of others) Exod 22:7; 22:10 (E), Est 9:10 +, בַּחַלָּמִישׁ‎ Job 28:9; with אֶל‎ person against Gen 22:12 (E), 2Sam 18:12, עַל‎ person 1Kin 13:4, etc.; אֶל‎ of thing (for good) 2Sam 6:6 (יָד‎ omitted); from outside; inward, Song 5:4 (מִן‎ local); absolute Job 30:24 (read טֹבֵעַ‎ for בְּעִי‎ Di Bi Bu). + infinitive purpose 1Sam 22:17, 17; 2Sam 1:14; 1Chr 13:9; + verbfin.active Gen 3:22 (J) Deut 25:11; Judg 15:15; +; ׳שׁ אֶצְבַּע‎ Isa 58:9, in token of scorn; with accusative of rod 1Sam 14:27; מַגָּל שִׁלְחוּ‎ Joel 4:13 stretch out (the) sickle.

b. ׳י‎ subject, accusative hand, + אֶל‎ person against Exodus 24:(E), compare (עַל‎) Psa 138:7; + finite verb active Exod 3:20 (JE), 9:15(J), Job 1:11; 2:5; in favour, Jer 1:9, absolute Psa 144:7 (מִן‎ local), also (passive) Ezek 2:9 and accusative יָד תַּבְנִית‎), 8:3.

c. accusative hand, subject angel, + accusative of location, infinitive purpose 2Sam 24:16, cherub, אֶל‎ of thing, מִן‎ local Ezek 10:7; adversary, אֶל‎ person Job 1:12; subject angel, accusative rod Judg 6:21.

d. stretched out, slender, of tree Gen 49:21 (poem in J), see I. אֵלָה‎ above.

e. perhaps extend, direct, accusative of thing Ezek 8:17 (see זְמוֺרָה‎ above, also conjectures in Toy Krae).

4 rarely send away (see Pi`el): human subject, accusative of person Judg 11:38 ( + accusative temporal), Gen 28:5 (P).

5 let loose (see

Pi`el), perhaps only Psa 50:19 (figurative) thy mouth hast thou let loose in evil.

Niph`al Infinitive absolute. סְפָרִים וְנִשְׁלוֺחַ‎ = letters were sent (Ges§ 113z gg) Est 3:13 ( + אֶל‎ person, בְּיַד‎ agent., infinitive purpose).

Pi`el266 Perfect3masculine singular שִׁלַּח‎ Exod 8:28 +, suffix שִׁלַּחֲךָ‎ 1Sam 20:22, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יְשַׁלַּח‎ Jer 3:1 +, יְשַׁלֵּ֑חַ‎ Isa 45:13; Prov 6:14; 1singular suffix אֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ‎ Gen 32:27, אֲשַׁלְּחֶךָּ‎ 2Sam 11:12; 1Kin 20:34, etc.; Imperative masculine singular שַׁלַּךְ‎ Exod 4:23, +, etc.; Infinitive absolute Deut 22:7; 1Kin 11:22; construct שַׁלַּךְ‎ Gen 8:10 +, שַׁלֵּ֑ךְַ‎ Exodus 7:27; +, etc.; Participle מְשַׁלֵחַ‎ 43:4 +, etc.; —

1 send off, away, human subject:

a. accusative of person + ל‎ location Josh 24:28 (E), Judg 7:8; 1Sam 10:23 +; + ל‎ person Jer 48:12; + הּ‎+? Judg 12:9 and (c. infinitive purpose) Gen 28:6 (P); accusative of goat, לַעֲזָאזֵל‎ Lev 16:10 (ה‎- locative), 16:26; send out, different ways, accusative of person, ב‎ location Judg 19:29; 20:6; send into exile, ׳י‎ subject, with מִן‎ local Jer 24:5, ה‎+? 29:20.

d. send off, give a 'send-off' (sometimes escort part way), accusative of person, Gen 18:16; 24:59; 31:27 (all J), 1Sam 9:26; 2Kin 5:24; 6:23.

2. a. send away, subject ׳י‎, accusative of person Gen 19:29 (J; מִתּוֺךְ‎), 1Kin 9:7 (מְּנֵי מֵעַל‎).

b. give over, accusative of person Psa 81:13 (ב‎ of evil).

c. cast out, accusative of person Jer 28:16 (מֵעַלמְּֿנֵי‎), Lev 18:24; 20:23 (both מִמְּנֵי‎).

Exodus), 1Sam 5:11; with accusative of bird Gen 8:7-8, (+ מֵאִתּוֺ‎) +; + הַשָּׂדֶה‎ Lev 14:7, compare 14:53 (both P); = let loose, accusative of beast, Exod 22:4 (E), Lev 16:22 (ב‎ location); accusative of bridle Job 30:11 (figurative); metaphor of strife Prov 6:14, 19; 16:28; let loose waters, subject ׳י‎, Job 12:15.

2); compare of locks (מֶּרַע‎) Ezek 44:20 = let grow long.

פדות.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

or po or po מֹּה‎58, and (Ezekiel 40-41, 23 out of 35 t.) מּוֺ‎, also Job 38:11b מֹּא‎,

Gen 19:12 מֹּה מִילְֿךָ עֹד‎ whom hast thou still here ? 22:5 מֹּה לָכֶם שְׁבוּ‎, 40:15; Num 22:8; 32:16; Deut 5:28; 12:8; Judg 4:20 אִישׁ מֹּה הֲיֵשׁ‎, 2Kin 3:11, etc.; asked in some surprise, Judg 18:3 פֹה מַהלְּֿךָ‎ = what is thy business here ? simil. 1Kin 19:9, 13; Isa 22:16; 52:5 מַהלִּֿיפֹֿה וְעַתָּה‎. compare the synonym כֹּה בָּזֶה,‎

פלדת.def:
the‎, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.

הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ‎ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHMEpigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ‎) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges§ 126 Ew§ 277): —

1 joined with substantives:

a. to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ‎ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל‎ 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים‎ i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן‎ the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן‎, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן‎ (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן‎), הַיַּרְדֵּן‎ (but not הָאַרְנֹן‎), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל,‎ the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה‎ the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר,‎ the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה,‎ '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה‎ 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל‎ 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל,‎ (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,‎.

b. with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור‎ the greater light, הקטן המאור‎ the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו‎ = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר‎ the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן‎ the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל‎ the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן‎ the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר‎ the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה‎ the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה‎ the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

c. with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם‎ to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה‎ to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה‎ this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם‎ this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר‎ the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר‎ the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר‎ 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא‎ = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה‎, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית‎.

d. it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ‎ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר‎ literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה‎, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ‎, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל‎ a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת‎ hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן‎ with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז‎ (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז‎ was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר‎, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט‎ on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל‎ with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה‎ a girl (compare Dr1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or

d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

e. with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,‎; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה‎, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת‎, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר‎, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם‎, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף,‎ etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף,‎ etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף,‎ etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף‎ and הבהמה‎, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם‎, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן‎ and הַשֵּׁכָר‎, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ‎, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן‎, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

f. in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים,‎ like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק‎, 5:28 כַּצַּר‎ and כַּסּוּפָה‎, 10:14 כַּקֵּן‎, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה‎ (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר‎; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ‎ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה‎ Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא‎) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא‎ Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי‎ Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי‎ Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר‎ Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור‎ Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר‎ as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר‎, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר‎), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר‎, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע‎ like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ‎ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ‎ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ‎ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל‎ Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל‎ Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ‎ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ‎ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל‎ 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל‎ like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ‎ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ‎ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן‎ Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן‎ like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם‎ like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,‎, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים‎. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

g. prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן‎ all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת‎ all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר‎ of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ‎ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט‎ those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ‎, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף‎; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב‎; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית‎; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא‎ the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי‎ the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה‎ woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי‎ the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי‎ 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי‎ Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי‎ the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

h. with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר‎; הזה החסד‎ 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את‎ Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק‎ Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה‎ Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת‎ Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת‎ Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר‎), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה‎ Isa 11:5b (contr. va) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה‎ Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים‎ Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה‎ Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר‎ Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת‎ Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע‎ Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה‎ Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ‎ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים‎, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,‎, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ‎, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד‎ Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח‎ Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק‎ 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה‎ also always); בֶּאֱמֶת‎ and בֶּאֱמוּנָה‎ always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר‎ Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב‎, not הַכָּזָב‎) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר‎ 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם‎ Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם‎); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן‎ (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון‎), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט‎ Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט‎ Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ‎ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה‎, (but never הַחכמה‎ in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה‎, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה‎ (but never הַבִּינָה‎); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה‎ (but הַתְּבוּנָה‎ only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא‎ Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ‎, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה‎ German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה‎ (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי‎ into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי‎ (so always: never בְחשׁך‎). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

i. to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך‎ as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן‎ Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל‎, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ‎, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים‎, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר‎, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת‎ O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי‎ (Dr§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ‎; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם‎; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ‎; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם‎; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר‎; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם‎ etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע‎; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.

2 With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,‎): namely

a. (so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך‎ = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ‎, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר‎, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים‎ = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ‎, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם‎); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ‎ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי‎ (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי‎), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ‎ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה‎): see Dr§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר‎ he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים‎ which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים‎ who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr§ 135. 7).

b. (rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום‎, 2:3 השׁביעי יום‎, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא‎ entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר‎ Zech 14:10; חָצֵר‎ court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל‎, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ‎ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה‎ all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ‎, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ‎, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ‎ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ‎ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים‎ many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב‎ the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5‎ Co omit הגוים‎), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה‎). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד‎ the evil inclination): see further Dr§ 209.

c. with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא‎ not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי‎ my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ‎ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr§ 135. 7).

3 The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא‎ that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר‎, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל‎ and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין‎ in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה‎ (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ‎, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה‎, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨‎, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה‎, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה‎): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה,‎ compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה‎), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה‎, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה‎ (compare Ew§ 331 b Ges138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ‎ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה‎ and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: WAG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew§ 290 d, Ges§ 127 R. 4, also Dr§ 190-1.

פלה.def:
H6213. asah

I. עָשָׂה‎2622 verb do, make (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew; MI23, 26 עשתי‎, l.3; l.9 ואעש‎, l.24 Imperative עשו‎; Old Hebrew proper name מעשיהו אלעשה, עשיו,‎; not Aramaic, and not certainly found in South Semitic languages; on Sabean see especially DHMSB Berl. Akkadian 1886, 849); —

Qal2524 Perfect3masculine singular Gen 3:1 +, suffix עָשָׂהוּ‎ Hosea 8:6 +; 3 feminine singular עָֽשְׂתָה‎ Deut 22:21 +, וְעָשָׂת‎ consecutive Lev 25:21; 2masculine singular עָשִׂיתָ‎ Gen 3:14 +, etc.; Imperfect3masculine singular יַעֲשֶׂה‎ 18:25 +, וַיַּעֲשֶׂה‎ 1Kin 16:25 3t., וַיַּעַשׂ‎ Isa 5:2 +; יַעֲשֵׂה‎ 64:3, 2masculine singular תַּעֲשֶׂה‎ 1Sam 10:8, תַּעֲשֵׂה‎ Gen 26:29; Josh 7:9, jussive (with אַל‎) תַּעַשׂ‎ Gen 22:12 +, תַּעֲשֵׂה‎ 2Sam 13:12; Jer 40:16 Qr (Kt תַּעַשׂ‎); 1 singular אֶעֱשֶׂה‎ Gen 2:18 +, וָאֶעֱשֶׂה‎ Ezek 20:14; Dan 8:27, וָאַעַשׂ‎ Deut 10:3-4t. Ezekiel; etc.; Imperative masculine singular עֲשֵׂה‎ Judg 10:15 +; feminine singular עֲשִׂי‎ Jer 6:26 +, etc.; Infinitive absolute עָשׂה‎ 44:17 +; עָשׂוֺ‎ 7:5 2t. (4:18 van d. H. עָשׂוּ‎); construct עֲשׂוֺת‎ Gen 2:4 +, עֲשׂה‎ 50:20 2t., עֲשׂוֺ‎ 31:28, suffix עֲשׂתוֺ‎ 41:32 +, עֲשׂהוּ‎ Exod 18:18, etc.; Participle active עשֶֹׁה‎ Isa 5:5 +, suffix הָעשֹׁוֺ‎ Job 40:19 (but see below); plural עשִֹׁים‎ Gen 24:49 +; suffix עשָֹׁ֑י‎ Job 35:10 (yet see Ges§ 124k), etc.; passive עָשׂוּי‎ Exod 3:16 +, הֶעָשׂוּ‎ Job 41:25 (Ges§ 75k); feminine עֲשׂוּיָה‎ Ezek 21:20 +, etc.; —

I. 1. do (1560 + t.):

a. (1) with accusative active Gen 3:14 (J) 20:10 (E) + often; do right in eyes of ׳י‎ 2Kin 12:3; 14:13 +, evil 8:18, 27 + (compare I. עַיִן‎

3c); do God's commands, statutes, etc., Deut 16:12; 30:8; Num 15:39 (P); ׳ע חַיִל‎ 1Sam 14:48 + do might, i.e. mightily, valiantly; Proverbs 31:39 do efficiency, i.e. efficiently; = commit (offence) Lev 20:13 (H), Deut 20:18; followed by מִן‎ particle, מֵהֵנָּה מֵאַחַת וְעָשָׂה‎ Lev 4:2 and shall do a single one of them (things prohibited; see מִן‎ 3b (d)), compare י מִכָּלמִֿצְוֺת אַחַת ׳וְעָשׂוּ‎ 4:13; 4:22; 5:17 (all P); do = perform a work, with accusative of congnate meaning with verb מַעֲשֶׂה‎ Exod 18:20; 23:12 (E), also (׳י‎ subject) Deut 11:7; Dan 9:14; Eccl 3:11; with accusative מְלָאכָה‎ Gen 2:2 (twice in verse) (J), Exod 20:9-10, = Deut 9:13 (10 Words); with accusative דְּרָכֶיךָ‎ Isa 58:13; ׳ע עַל מְלוּכָה‎ 1Kin 21:7 = exercise sovereignty over; of ׳י‎ performing signs (אֹתֹת‎) Josh 24:17 (E), Num 14:11, 22 (JE), Deut 11:3, so Moses Exod 4:17 and (מֹפְתִים‎) 4:21. (2) do something to one (ל‎ person) Gen 20:9 (E), Judg 9:56 +; with עַל‎ reflexive Jer 26:19 do evil against ourselves; especially ׳י‎ subject, with לְ‎, do good to Exod 18:9 (E), 2 Kings 8:66, or evil Gen 42:28 (E); in phrase so may God do to me, etc. 1Sam 3:17; 2Kin 6:31 + (see יסף‎

Hiph`il 1.). (3) do something for one (ל‎ person) Gen 30:31; 1Kin 11:8 +, direct object omitted 1Sam 20:4; + ל‎ of thing Judg 21:7, 16 what shall we do for them, for wives ? with עַל‎ person Neh 5:19; with dativus ethicus [dative of interest] (ל‎) 1Sam 10:7; with לְ‎, of ׳י‎ doing kindness for 22:3; executing vengeance for Judg 11:36 (+ מִן‎ of enemy); ׳י‎ doing a sign (אוֺת‎) for 6:17 (elsewhere לְ אוֺת נָתַן‎), compare לְטוֺבָה אוֺת עֲשֵׂהעִֿמִּי‎ Psa 86:17. (4) do something (in relation or intercourse) wilth (אֵת‎ person), ׳י‎ subject Deut 1:30 all that he did with you, 10:21 (compare Psa 86:17 above), human subject 2Chr 24:24 (object שְׁפָטִים‎), Ruth 2:11. (5) seldom with ב‎, usually of executing judgment upon 1Sam 28:18; Isa 48:14, more Generally Est 1:15 what shall we do with the queen ? also, subject ׳י‎, Ezek 25:11; 28:26; Psa 149:7; 149:9; Num 33:4 (on false gods); in good sense, ׳ע בּ ׳חֲסָדִים‎ Neh 13:14. (6) of ׳י‎ doing the justice (מִשְׁמַּט‎) of any one, i.e. maintaining his cause 1Kin 8:45, 49; Psa 9:5. (7) with adverb do thus, כֹּה‎, Josh 6:14 (JE), according to, כְּ‎ Gen 6:22 (P), 18:21 (J), 1Kin 2:6; accusative as, כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ Gen 27:19 (J); Exod 1:17 (E) +; with בְּ‎ of manner, Judg 9:16a, Ezek 8:18; 25:15.

b. work for (ל‎ of thing) Gen 30:30 (J); with ל‎ person 1Sam 14:6; Ezek 29:20 (for ׳י‎); work in (ב‎) gold or other material 1Kin 7:14; 2Chr 2:6; 2:13; Exod 31:4-5, 35:32 (all P); with בָּהּ‎ (i.e. בָּעֲבֹדָה‎) 5:9 (J) in toil; work with (עִם‎) God 1Sam 14:45, so probably of God's working with (אֵת‎) Moses and Aaron 12:6 (usually appoint); with אֵת‎ with (of person in whose company, in whose field Ruth 2:19 (twice in verse) (gleaning); work כַּמֶּיהָ בְּחֵפֶץ‎ Prov 31:13; without preposition Exod 36:1; Neh 3:28.

2 deal with, with עִם‎, 2Chr 2:2; Dan 1:13 (כַּאֲשֶׁר‎ accusative as); with אֵת‎, Ezek 20:44; Psa 109:21; Ezek 22:14; Zeph 3:19 (perhaps; Gr Now insert כָּלָה‎, see

II 1 g), + כְּ‎ Jer 21:2, + בְּ‎ of manner Ezek 23:25, 29; with לְ‎ person + בְּ‎ 25:12; with בְּ‎ person, Jer 18:23; Dan 11:7, + כְּ‎ according to Neh 9:24; Est 3:11.

3 often in phrase, do kindness (חֶסֶד‎) with: with עִם (עִמָּדִ)‎ Gen 19:19; 24:12; 12:14 (J), Judg 1:24; 8:35; 1Sam 15:6; 2Sam 2:5; 10:2 = 1Chr 19:2 +; with עַל‎, 1Sam 20:8 (but read עִם‎ Vrss We Dr and others); absolute, Psa 109:16; object חֶסֶד‎ + אֱמֶת‎, with עִם‎, Josh 2:14 (JE) Judg 9:19; 2Sam 2:6; with אֵת‎ with, Gen 24:49; 32:11; 47:29 (all J); with לְ‎, Exod 20:6 = Deut 5:10; 2Sam 22:51 = Psalm 18:51; so ׳ע טוֺב‎, with עִם‎, Gen 26:29 (J), compare Judg 8:35; 9:16; with אֵת‎ with, 1Sam 24:19; 2Sam 2:6.

4 absolute act, act with effect, especially of ׳י‎, 1Kin 8:32, 39; Jer 14:7; Ezek 20:9, 14, 22; Psalm 22:32; Psa 37:5; Psalm 52:11; Dan 9:19; of men 2Chr 31:21; Dan 8:12, 24; 11:28, 30, 32; with ל‎ of person Ezek 31:11.

II. 1. make (670 + t.):

a. with object concrete, ark Gen 8:6, altar 13:4, idols Judg 18:24, 31 +, etc.

b. often of God's making (creating) Gen 3:1 (J), 1:7, 16, 25 (P), Neh 9:6; Job 9:9; Prov 8:26; 2Chr 2:11; Psa 95:5 +; making man 100:3; 119:73 (made by God's hands), in the womb Job 31:15 (twice in verse); making, constituting, nation Deut 26:19; 32:6, 15; participle suffix עשֵֹׁהוּ‎ his Maker Isa 17:7; Prov 14:31; 17:5 (הָעשֹׁוֺ‎ Job 40:19 is improbable, most read הֶעָשָׂוּי‎, with various interpretation of following words); עשֶֹׁךָ‎ Isa 51:13, עשֵֹׁנִי‎ Job 32:23 (Ginsb; Job 32:22 van d. H. Baer), עשֵֹׁנוּ‎ Psa 95:6; so apparently plural participle עשָֹׁ֑י‎ Job 35:10, עשַֹׁיִךְ‎ Isa 54:5 (Ges§ 124k explanation as sg.).

c. make something, with לְ‎ reflexive, make for thee Exod 20:4; Deut 9:12; 10:1 +, for (ל‎) another 1Sam 2:19; 2Sam 7:11; 1Kin 2:24 +; object מִשְׁתֶּה‎ banquet Gen 40:20; Est 5:4, also (no ל‎) Gen 29:22 (E) Judg 14:10; Est 5:5, 12 and (figurative, ׳י‎ subject) Isa 25:6; with ל‎ of thing, Deut 22:8; with ל‎ of animal Gen 33:17 (J).

d. make a name (שֵׁם‎) for oneself (ל‎) 2Sam 7:9; 1Chr 17:8, also (no ל‎) 2Sam 8:13; a new heart for oneself (ל‎) Ezek 18:31.

e. make war with (אֶת‎) Gen 14:2; Josh 11:18 (D); with עִם‎, Deut 20:12, 20; 1Chr 5:10, 19; absolute 22:8; with ל‎ reflexive Prov 24:6; participle מִלְחָמָה עשֵֹׁה‎2Chr 11:1; 26:11, 13; make peace, with ל‎ person Josh 9:15 (J); ׳ע בְרָכָה אִתִּי‎ 2Kin 18:31 make an agreement with me.

f. with ׳ע בּ ׳מֶּרֶץ ב,‎ Judg 21:15 ׳י‎ brought a catastrophe upon (compare פרץ‎).

g. with 2 accusative, make something out of (accusative mater.) Exod 25:18; 28:13; 37:17, 24; Song 3:10; Deut 10:3 +; make something into something (Ges§ 117ii) Hosea 8:4; Gen 27:9; Judg 17:4; Num 11:8; 17:3; Psa 104:4; make something כָּלָה‎, i. e. utterly destroy it Nahum 1:8; Zeph 1:18; Ezek 20:17; Neh 9:31; c. passive participle as 2nd accusative Exod 38:7 they made it לֻחֹת נְבוּב‎ hollow with boards, 39:9; but also with accusative + לְ‎, Hosea 2:10 gold they made into (ל‎) the Baal, Judg 8:27; Exod 27:3 (P), Deut 9:14; Jer 37:15; Ezek 4:9; Isa 44:17, 19; make something for (ל‎ person), + מִן‎ of material Song 3:9.

2 produce, yield: of grain, yielding meal Hosea 8:7 (twice in verse), vineyard, grapes Isa 5:2 (twice in verse); 5:4 (twice in verse); 5:10, tree, fruit 2Kin 19:30 = Isa 37:31; Hosea 9:16; Jer 12:2; 17:8; Ezek 17:23 (all figurative), Gen 1:11-12, (P); branches Job 14:9 and (figurative) Ezek 17:8; land, fruit Lev 25:21 compare Hab 3:17, absolute Gen 41:47; of seed Isa 5:10, vine, shoots Ezek 17:6 (figurative); of cows, yielding milk Isa 7:22; hippop. producing fat Job 15:27.

3 prepare, especially of dressing and cooking food, Gen 18:7-8, Judg 6:19; 13:5; 1Sam 25:18 (passive), 2Sam 12:4 (twice in verse); Gen 27:14, 17, 31; 2Sam 13:5, 7; 1Kin 17:12; Exod 12:39 (+ ל‎ reflexive); a bullock for sacrifice (see below) 1Kin 18:23, 25, 26; גוֺלָה כְּלֵי‎ Ezek 12:3 (+ ל‎ reflexive); a chamber Neh 13:7; prepare to build (+ ל‎ person and infinitive).

4 make offering, e.g. עוֺלָה‎ Judg 13:16; Jer 33:18; Lev 16:24, וָזֶבַח עוֺלָה‎ 2Kin 5:17 (+ ל‎ of deity), הַחַטָּאת‎ Lev 14:19, אִשֶּׁה‎ Num 15:3, 14, various offerings 1Kin 8:64; Lev 9:22; Ezek 45:17; 46:2 +; + ׳לי‎ to ׳י‎ Lev 17:9 +; also with accusative of thing sacrificed (perhaps originally prepare or provide, see above) Ezek 43:25 (twice in verse); 46:15; Lev 14:30; 15:15, 30; 16:9; Num 6:11, 17; Psa 66:15 (+ ל‎ of deity) +; absolute = offer sacrifice Exod 10:25 (E + ׳לי‎), to (ל‎) heathen gods 2Kin 17:32.

5 attend to, put in order: pare (the nails) Deut 21:12; wash (feet) 2Sam 19:25; trim (beard) v.19:25 (compare French faire la barbe, German die Haare machen).

6 observe, celebrate, religious festival, e.g. passover Exod 12:48; Num 9:4, 6, 13; Josh 5:10, also (+ ׳לי‎) Exod 12:48; Num 9:10, 14 (all P), Deut 16:1 +; sabbath Exod 31:16; Deut 5:15; feast of weeks 16:10, booths 16:13, Purim Est 9:21, 27, etc.

8 appoint priests 1Kin 12:31; 13:33; 2Chr 2:17 (all + מִן‎ source), a feast 1Kin 12:32-33, (+ ל‎ person); ordain a sacrifice Num 28:6, a festal day Psa 118:24; institute, וְיִדְּעֹנִי אוֺב‎ ghost and familiar spirit 2Kin 21:6 2Chr 33:6 (compare DrDeut 18:11).

9 bring about, of ׳י‎s effecting a deliverance Exod 14:13 (לָכֶם‎), 1Sam 11:13; 2Sam 23:10 (insert also || 1Chr 11:13 Dr), 11:12; cause, followed by clause with שֶׁ‎ Eccl 3:14.

10 use, ׳וְע לִמְלַאכְתּוֺ‎ 1Sam 8:16; passive Exod 38:24.

11 spend, pass, days of life Eccl 6:12.

d. be done upon, against (ב‎) Dan 9:12.

c. be prepared, of food Exod 12:16; Lev 6:14; 7:9 (all P), Neh 5:18 (twice in verse).

d. be offered, מִנְחָה‎ Lev 2:8, 11, kid Num 28:15, 24.

f. be used + ל‎ of thing Lev 7:24 (P); 13:51 (P) Ezek 15:5 (twice in verse).
